headline: High-risk workspace leakage and cascading errors: Gemini CLI can write/read local files while Notion AI ingests workspace content and sends it to vendor backends.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can write filesystem content and use MCP, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and knowledge-base content. If Gemini writes attacker-controlled text into shared files or pages that Notion later summarizes, instructions can be smuggled through the shared workspace. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI writes prompt-like text into a file or page that Notion AI later reads
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or answer from that shared content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict Gemini CLI to a dedicated directory not indexed by Notion
Add a manual review step before Notion AI consumes Gemini-generated files
Use separate workspaces for code and knowledge content
Disable MCP sources that can write shared content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction stripping before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can read local files and shell environment, and Notion AI can access workspace pages and send content to Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers. If sensitive code or secrets are copied into workspace pages or shared files, both agents can expose them across different backends. The pair has no documented isolation preventing this.
conditions: IF secrets or source code are placed in pages or files accessible to both agents
IF Notion AI processes that content through vendor backends
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace pages
Store code and credentials in separate repositories or vaults
Limit Notion AI access to non-sensitive pages
Rotate any secrets that were copied into shared content
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before Notion ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has filesystem write and git modification capabilities, while Notion AI has shared workspace state across all members and can act on workspace content. Their mutable surfaces overlap indirectly through files and shared content, so concurrent edits can conflict or overwrite each other. No locking or coordination primitive is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI edits files or git state that are mirrored into Notion workspace content
IF multiple instances operate on the same shared page or file set without locking
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource
Use branch-per-agent workflows for git changes
Freeze shared pages during automated edits
Review diffs before syncing content between systems
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking across shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate and modify files, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Gemini-produced text is imported into Notion and then treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into summaries, decisions, or downstream actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI writes analysis or facts into files that Notion AI later uses as source material
IF Notion AI presents that material without independent verification
mitigations: Require human review of Gemini outputs before Notion ingestion
Mark machine-generated pages clearly
Cross-check critical claims against primary sources
Limit Notion AI to retrieval, not action-taking, for imported content
requires-engineering: add source-verification scoring before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI can touch local source code, files in cwd, and shell environment, while Notion AI handles workspace pages and sends content to vendor backends. If regulated data is copied from local development artifacts into Notion, residency and retention obligations may diverge between the two services. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data from local files or code comments is copied into Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency constraints
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Notion pages
Use redacted excerpts instead of raw artifacts
Confirm workspace policy before syncing content
Delete sensitive pages after use
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
